Dear Folks: A kind soul has submitted a summary of the Manifesto for the 
time-impaired who haven't read it. I was going to do this myself as a lot 
of people don't really know what it's all about. Hope it uploads 
successfuly! --Laura

-----

=================================
Industrial Society and Its Future
=================================

Industrial society makes life unfulfilling.

Modern leftists have inferiority complexes and are oversocialized.
They identify with oppressed groups and they vent their hostility
through unyielding activism rather than diplomatic negotiating.  They
don't emphasize self-reliance and initiative.  They have an overdeveloped
sense of self-shame.  They rationalize their hate for society by saying 
that society does not uphold up principles like racial equality.  They want 
minorities to be just like white people.  The ethnic culture that they 
defend (music, food, church) is superficial.  They want minorities to 
succeed in the white work culture (get a good education and climb the 
status ladder).

People have a need for the power process: have goals, expend effort to
attain them and achieve at least some of these goals.  Some people also
require autonomy.  People set up surrogate activities so that they can
pursue goals if all their physical needs are taken care of.  Science,
athletics, art, social activism, climbing the corporate ladder are all
examples of surrogate activities.  Surrogate goals are not as satisfying
as real goals.  People need autonomy in choosing and pursuing their
goals in order to be satisfied.

In general, primitive societies didn't have the problems caused by 
modern man being unable to experience the power process.  These problems
include depression, anxiety, guilt, inferiority feelings and hostility.
Crowding, rapid change and the breakdown of communities also are sources
of social problems.  Modern man has change imposed on him; he does not
instigate change.

In modern society most human drives are either easily satisfied or impossible
to satisfy.  There are few that require serious effort to satisfy and these
are usually social needs (sex, love and status) or artificial (such as 
consumer desires created by advertizing).

Threats to modern man are man-made while threats to primitive man are 
mostly from nature.

Modern society is permissive about things that don't threaten the system
such as sex and religion.

People adjust by pursuing artificial drives such as status, material
goods, athletics, and hobbies.  Some people identify with a larger 
organization such as the government and strive to accomplish goals that 
serve the organization.  But for most people the need for the power process 
is not fully satisfied.

Science is a surrogate activity, not a way to satisfy curiosity or to
benefit humanity.  Scientists pursue their work to satisfy the power
process.

Freedom is the opportunity to go through the power process with real goals,
not the artificial ones of surrogate activities, and without interference.

History has long term trends that can be perturbed by things like reform
movements but it will soon revert to their long term course.  A new society
can't be planned on paper.  Revolution is necessary because reforms can't
alter long-term trends.  Utopian societies don't work because society is
too complex and unpredictable to plan.

Technology is incompatible with freedom.  Reforming technology won't work.
It is unnatural to force adolescents to spend long hours at a desk studying.
Modern medicine allows genetic misfits to survive.  Genetic engineering will
allow the upper-class to impose its values on the genetic makeup of people.

Technology is a more powerful social force than the aspiration for freedom.
People are forced to adopt technological advances such as automobiles 
because societal changes to require the new technology.  The same thing
will happen with genetic engineering.  People will be forced to adopt 
genetic engineering just like they were forced to adopt the automobile.

Fighting the encroachment of technology on freedom is not as rewarding
an activity as developing new technology so reformers are at a disadvantage.
It is possible, though, that during the next several decades the amount of
stress produced by technological advances will create so much alienation,
hostility and rebellion that the aspiration for freedom will surpass the
development of technology as a social force.  When industrial society becomes
sick the opportunity should be seized and it should be killed off.

Revolution can be easier than reform because it promises larger changes and
inspires greater commitment.

Modern technology is able to change people so that they adapt to the
stresses of modern life.  People take drugs to take away the unhappiness
caused by the structure of society.  Other methods of controlling human
behavior include surveillance, computer databases, propaganda and 
entertainment.  Psychotherapy teaches people to adapt and conform to the
system.

If a person is genetically reengineered so that he will not have criminal
tendencies he is actually being altered to adapt to the system.  In primitive
societies the crime rate is much lower so we can assume that it is modern
society that is making people into criminals.  Technology will make it
easier to control and manipulate people's behavior through drugs, genetic
engineering and possibly neural stimulation.  If advances in these techniques
are not developed in the next 40 to 100 years then society will probably
break down.  For a revolution to succeed the stresses within society must
be heightened and an anti-technology ideology must be developed.  The
revolution will have to destroy the factories and burn the technical books.

Computer scientists may succeed in making intelligent machines that run
society.  The machines may not even require human oversight in which case
society will be at the mercy of the machines.  Society could drift into
dependence on the machines by relying on them for decision making that
becomes increasingly complex.  Or the machines may be controlled by a 
tiny elite that see the masses as superfluous.  If the elite consist of 
soft-hearted liberals they will see that everyone's physical needs are met
and that everyone has an interesting, wholesome hobby and that any 
dissatisfied individuals receive an appropriate treatment.  Life will be
purposeless and people will be reduced to the status of domestic animals.

Machines may not become this advanced.  People may be pushed into the service
industries to give them busy work (shining shoes, driving taxis, waiting on
tables).

The revolution should promote wild nature as an ideal.  People will become
hunters, herdsmen, fishermen or peasants.  The ideology should be promoted
in two ways.  One way would be rational and intellectually respectable and
appeal to intelligent people.  The other way would be simpler and more
unambiguous but not so inflammatory and manipulative as to alienate the core
of intelligent people.  To win over the public, revolutionaries must be 
careful not to criticize or blame the public.  The revolution is economic
and technological not political.  The revolutionaries should not try to 
take political power now because they would have to implement anti-growth 
that would alienate the public.  The revolution must be international so
that the threat of other countries having technological superiority is 
removed.  NAFTA and GATT are good because they promote international economic 
interdependence that will make it easier to destroy the system on a worldwide
basis.

Revolutionaries should not pursue other goals like social justice because
these struggles will make them dependent on technology.  

Revolutionaries should have lots of children because social attitudes are
inherited.

Small-scale technology can be used by small communities without outside
assistance unlike organization-dependent technology.  The latter kind of
technology can regress, for example when the Roman Empire declined.  Thus,
once industrial society is torn down it will take centuries to rebuild it.

In the late Middle Ages, Europe, the Islamic World, India and China were
equally advanced but only Europe became technologically advanced.  Thus,
industrial society is not inevitable.

The revolution must be anti-leftist because leftism is collective and 
dependent on technology.  Leftists are untrustworthy revolutionary allies
because historically they have turned on those who cooperated with them.
Leftism is totalitarian.  Leftists like to restrict and coerce individuals
and impose their morality on others.  Leftists are True Believers.  Some
leftists are tolerant of others beliefs but the general trend is intolerance.
